svg.aria-label: The native-oracle sweep of the stress run: all 14 exhaustive items complete, and 1,356,316,228,303 cases in all, of which 30.6% exercised the tile and the rest ran in libcft's host code on the box's CPU; no case disagreed.
svg.title: The native-oracle sweep of the stress run: all 14 exhaustive items complete, and 1,356,316,228,303 cases in all, of which 30.6% exercised the tile and the rest ran in libcft's host code on the box's CPU; no case disagreed.
svg.text: What the sweep covered, and what of it ran on the tile
Only some sweep operations exercise the card's tile: divide and square root, roundToIntegral and scaleB, which libcft
composes from the tile's opcodes. The rest - nextUp, nextDown, logB, class, the conversions, remainder - run in
libcft's host code on the box's CPU, and the tile does no work for them. Every figure below keeps the two apart.
the 14 exhaustive items: share of 2^32 covered
cases checked against the CPU's own answers, cumulative
slice rate by operation: cases per second a job, median, by image
quad (a job a tile, four at once)
14 of the 14 exhaustive items finished: 60,129,542,144 encodings, 10 x 2^32 through the tile (sqrt32 and rint32, five attributes each) and
4 x 2^32 in host code (nextup32, nextdown32, logb32, class32). The random items split the same way, 25 on the tile and 29 in host code. 0
cases disagreed, tile or host. A 'case' is what each tool's verdict counts, so one input can be several cases (the conversions).
